method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the 'Zoster (herpes zoster)' chapter of the Australian Immunisation Handbook, retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: Free to read but NOT openly licensed -- health.gov.au states 'all other rights are reserved'. Quoted with attribution on the same footing as the Stroke Foundation, Kidney Health Australia and NHFA/CSANZ sources already in this compendium.

claims.claim: **All immunocompetent people aged 50 and over are recommended zoster vaccine.**
claims.source_text: All people aged ≥50 years who are immunocompetent are recommended to receive zoster vaccine .
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Zoster (herpes zoster)', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/zoster-herpes-zoster, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **The lifetime risk of shingles for someone who lives to 80 is around 50%**, higher again if immunocompromised.
claims.source_text: The lifetime risk of herpes zoster for people who live to 80 years of age is around 50%. The risk is higher in those who are immunocompromised.
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Zoster (herpes zoster)', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/zoster-herpes-zoster, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.source_text: People who are immunocompetent are recommended to receive a 2-dose schedule of Shingrix, 2-6 months apart, for the prevention of herpes zoster and associated complications.
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Zoster (herpes zoster)', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/zoster-herpes-zoster, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Immunocompromised: 2 doses of Shingrix 1–2 months apart** — a shorter interval.
claims.source_text: For people who are immunocompromised, 2 doses of Shingrix are recommended at an interval of 1-2 months.
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Zoster (herpes zoster)', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/zoster-herpes-zoster, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **No booster is currently recommended.** Current data show **good protection at 10 years after 2 doses**.
claims.source_text: There is currently no booster recommendation for zoster vaccine. Current data supports good protection at 10 years following 2 doses of Shingrix.
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Zoster (herpes zoster)', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/zoster-herpes-zoster, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Shingrix is funded under the NIP for all adults 65 and over, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people 50 and over, and selected groups 18 and over with moderate or severe immunocompromise.**
claims.source_text: Shingrix is funded under the National Immunisation Program (NIP) for all adults aged ≥65 years, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people aged ≥50 years and selected groups aged ≥18 years with moderate or severe immunocompromise.
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Zoster (herpes zoster)', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/zoster-herpes-zoster, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **People who had Zostavax can receive Shingrix** — Zostavax protection **wanes significantly from around 5 years**. Leave **at least 12 months** between them.
claims.source_text: People who have previously received Zostavax can receive Shingrix to increase their protection against herpes zoster, since protection using Zostavax wanes significantly from around 5 years after vaccination. … an interval of at least 12 months is recommended between receiving Zostavax and a subsequent dose of Shingrix.
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Zoster (herpes zoster)', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/zoster-herpes-zoster, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: Shingles is **reactivation of varicella-zoster virus** in someone who has had chickenpox, usually a **painful, self-limiting vesicular rash in a dermatomal distribution**.
claims.source_text: Herpes zoster, commonly known as shingles, is a reactivation of the varicella-zoster virus (VZV) in a person who has previously had varicella (chickenpox). Herpes zoster commonly presents as a painful, self-limiting vesicular rash in a dermatomal distribution.
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Zoster (herpes zoster)', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/zoster-herpes-zoster, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **80% have a prodrome 48–72 hours before the rash** — headache, photophobia, malaise, and itching, tingling or severe pain in the dermatome. The rash usually lasts **10–15 days**.
claims.source_text: 80% of cases have a prodromal phase 48-72 hours before the rash appears. … headache photophobia malaise itching, tingling or severe pain in the affected dermatome In most people, herpes zoster is an acute and self-limiting disease. The rash usually lasts 10-15 days.
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Zoster (herpes zoster)', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/zoster-herpes-zoster, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Post-herpetic neuralgia is the most common complication** — about **1 in 5 cases over 80**, compared with about 1 in 10 at younger ages. Complications are commoner in older and immunocompromised people.
claims.source_text: Complications occur more often in older people and people who are immunocompromised. … Post-herpetic neuralgia ( PHN ) is the most common complication of herpes zoster, but it occurs very infrequently in children and young adults.
